description: The costliest confusion this function can make. A card reporting that a group appointed a supplier names a buyer and a supplier; proposing the buyer would put a Canvas client or prospect into the competitor register, which eleven scanners then watch and name in their output.

cards.headline: Ridgeway Holdings appointed Northfield Analytics for group consolidation reporting
cards.so_what: A multi-entity group buying exactly what Canvas sells, from a supplier not in the register

expected_output.shape: single JSON object with keys horizon_days, candidates

rubric.condition: Zero occurrences of the exact string "Ridgeway Holdings" in any candidate's name field — it appointed a supplier, so it is a buyer and never a competitor.
The candidates array contains exactly 1 item — the card names one supplier not in known_competitors.
The candidate's evidence_headline exactly equals the input card's headline and its source_url exactly equals that card's source_url.

notes: Anchored to prompt.md hard rule 4 and the Method's "Who is the actor?" step. Hard rule 9 is why the rationale must describe the buyer generically if it refers to it at all.
